note:
1911 household schedules supplied by A. Hagues, filling the second half of the gaps the census-gap report found - the streets the record holds in 1891 and again in 1921 but not in 1901 or 1911.

**These are the householder's own schedules, not the enumerator's book.** The hand is the head of the household's, the signature at the foot is his, and the 1911 return asks a woman three questions no earlier census did: how long she has been married, how many children she has borne, and how many are still living. Those answers are kept here because nothing else in the record can supply them.

**Not named people_*.json on purpose**, so the importer never reads it. A reading I am unsure of carries [?].
source: 1911 census household schedules - transcribed by Claude from images supplied by A. Hagues

marriage.note: Married about 1878. The four are Harold (1879), Oswald (1882), Dorothea (1884) and Ursula (1891), and in 1911 all four were alive.

people.name: John Kenneth Varvill
people.note: Entered first as NEPHEW, struck through and altered to Visitor in the same hand.

households.note: Fills the 1911 half of the gap at 9 Newcastle Drive. The record holds John (#2128), Jessie (#2129) and Ursula in 1891 and again in 1921, so this is the middle of a run of at least thirty years in one house - the longest single tenure the gap report turned up on that street.

**THE GAP REPORT READ THIS AS TWO CHANGES OF FAMILY, AND IT IS ONE MAN MOVING HOUSE.** William Thomas Cartwright is at **1 Newcastle Drive** in 1891 and at **7** in 1901, 1911 and 1921. The report showed 1 Newcastle Drive as Cartwright-to-Copeland and 7 as Birkin-to-Cartwright, because it compares each house with itself and cannot see a household walk down its own street. His daughter Margaret Helen (#2153) carries both ends - 1891 at number 1, 1921 at number 7.

Mary J. Cartwright, his wife, is alive in 1901 and he is a widower here, so she died between the two returns. Vincent Henry (#1781, born 1883) is already in the record, at 2 Park Ravine by 1921.

people.name: Charlotte Loder
people.note: "Coachman" was written in her occupation column and struck out - her husband's trade carried down a line by mistake.

people.name: Stanley Loder
people.note: Charlotte gives three children in twenty-six years and she is 54, so an infant of eighteen months is very unlikely to be hers. A grandson, with the relationship column left blank.

households.note:
**SETTLED BY THE SCHEDULE COVER: *Back of 5 Newcastle Drive, The Park, Nottingham*.** The enumerator first wrote *Huntingdon Drive, The Park*, struck it through, and wrote the back of 5 underneath. So this is the coach house or stable flat behind **5 Newcastle Drive (#210)**, and A. Hagues had it right.

**My reasoning against it was worthless.** I argued from the schedule numbers - 14 at number 7, 18 at number 9, so 17 must fall between them - and an enumerator numbering back premises does not walk in a straight line. An address written on the paper beats an inference from the order of the paper every time.

**And the big house ties the two together.** 5 Newcastle Drive on the same night is Henry Gee's, and one of his four servants is **Fanny Charlotte Loder**, housemaid, 24, born Nottingham. Charles and Charlotte Loder are at the back with a son of 16. Fanny Charlotte is almost certainly their daughter: the coachman drives for the house, his wife keeps the coach house, and his daughter is in service in the front of the same property.

**Charlotte reports three children born alive and three still living.** Charles Wood, 16, and Fanny Charlotte, 24, are two of them. The third is elsewhere. Stanley, eighteen months, is not one of the three, so he is a generation down - whose is not on the paper.

people.name: Fanny Charlotte Loder
people.note: Almost certainly the daughter of Charles and Charlotte Loder at the back of this same house - schedule 17.

households.note:
Closes the 1911 half of the gap at 5 Newcastle Drive. The record holds **Thomas Hill**, hosiery manufacturer, there in 1891 and again in 1901 at 78 and widowed - and **Henry Gee** there in 1921. This puts Gee in the house by 1911, so the handover happened in that decade, and one hosiery manufacturer followed another into it.

Clara married about 1871 and bore two children, both living in 1911. Neither is in the house.

The cover gives the district numbers for the whole round: registration district 430, sub-district 1, **enumeration district 11** - which is the district to ask for if the rest of this 1911 round is wanted.

people.name: Mary Elizabeth Patterson
people.note: The record holds her as **Mary ELY Patterson**. This return writes it out as Elizabeth, and A. Hagues confirms it. Ely is a misreading of an abbreviated Elizth.

people.name: Emma Jarvis
people.note: The index reads the birthplace as "Bowns"; the record has Bourne from both 1891 and 1901, so Bourne it is.

people.name: Dora Muffel
people.note: The index reads "Manla Cambs". Manea is a Cambridgeshire village and the likeliest reading, but it is a guess at one letter and is marked as one.

households.note:
Closes the 1911 half of the gap at 1 Park Terrace. The record holds Mary Patterson there in 1891 and 1901 and a different family, the Cockburns, by 1921 - so this is the last census of her tenancy, at 82 and still keeping two servants.

**Emma Jarvis has been with her at least twenty years.** She is a servant in this house in 1891 at 31, in 1901 at 46 and here in 1911 at 51 - one woman across three returns, with the ages drifting as census ages do.

**And she is in the record twice because of that drift.** #3585 carries her 1891 row at born 1860; #4757 was created by the 1901 gap-round import at born 1855, because the page gave her age as 46. Five years apart, so neither the duplicates page nor variant_duplicates.py can see them - both test born years within two. This return gives 51, which agrees with #3585, so #3585 is the one to keep.
